abstract: Coloboma, a leading cause of childhood blindness, results from failed OFC. Variants in NTN1 (Netrin-1) are linked to coloboma and other tissue fusion defects, but how Netrin-1 influences epithelial fusion is unknown. We generated a germline NTN1 knockout chicken and analysed the fissure margins by immunofluorescence, in situ hybridisation, single-nucleus RNA sequencing and micro-CT. NTN1-/- embryos developed highly penetrant bilateral colobomas. The basement membrane (BM) was remodelled normally, yet pioneer cells at the optic fissure margins (OFMs) failed to detach and mix across the midline, retaining apical actin and displaying increased cadherin at the fissure edges. The ventral neural retina showed reduced apoptosis and became overgrown and folded at the fissure edges. These data show that Netrin-1 is required for pioneer cell detachment and this process is independent of BM remodelling. We found that pioneer cells in wild type (WT) OFMs were transiently exposed to fibronectin-rich periocular mesenchyme (POM) during BM remodelling, with fibronectin and laminin fragments localised at their exposed edges. Netrin-1 reduced adhesion of HEK293 cells to fibronectin in vitro, with and without laminin, but not to laminin alone, suggesting Netrin-1 mediates a substrate specific effect on cell adhesion. ITGB8 and ITGAV were co-expressed with NTN1 in pioneer cells, and Netrin-1 co-immunoprecipitated with ITGB8, identifying integrin V{beta}8 as a candidate Netrin-1 receptor in OFC. Integrin V{beta}8 with fibronectin typically activate canonical TGF{beta} signalling, however we found pSMAD2 was specifically absent from pioneer cell nuclei during fusion. In contrast, phosphorylated FAK was present in WT but not mutant fissures, indicating that Netrin-1 activates integrin mediated focal adhesion signalling in OFC. We propose that Netrin-1 and V{beta}8 enable pioneer cells to respond to transient POM-derived cues, such as fibronectin, triggering detachment and initiating fusion. This proposed mechanism could explain a direct role for the POM in mediating OFC.
